title: Rainfall-adjusted MODIS greenness trend, 2000 to 2025 (restrend_long_record 1.0.0)
description:
Precomputed result of recipe restrend_long_record 1.0.0 for Ait Bouguemez valley catchment: growing-season MODIS NDVI (MOD13Q1 v6.1, 250 m) regressed on antecedent CHIRPS v3.0 rainfall for each season 2000 to 2025, for the catchment and each terrain stratum, and the trend of what is left (the residual, a departure of greenness from the value expected from rainfall). Model estimate. Catchment, March to June greenness against September (previous year) to May rainfall, 26 seasons: +0.0015 NDVI per 100 mm of rain (95% interval -0.0017 to +0.0047, R squared 0.04). The rainfall slope interval does not lie entirely above zero, so the registered precondition is not met and no rainfall-adjusted trend is stated. Unadjusted greenness changed by +0.0091 NDVI per decade (95% interval +0.0046 to +0.0136, entirely above zero); the residual trend is stored for reference only.

The rainfall-adjusted residual still holds everything else that changes greenness: temperature, snow, irrigation, orchards and fields, grazing, fire, and sensor or orbit changes. It is not a measure of grazing impact or of degradation. Trend methods can miss real change: in simulations for southern Africa, 30 to 40% degradation was needed before a trend showed under a rainfall-driven increase, and the residual method broke down at about 20% degradation (Wessels et al. 2012). An interval that includes zero is not evidence of no change. Each 250 m MODIS pixel mixes surfaces; stratum values weight pixels by how much of the stratum falls inside them, so a mixed pixel counts toward more than one stratum. Rainfall comes from 5 km CHIRPS grid cells, not from gauges in the valley, and snowfall is counted with rain. Each stratum and window pair has its own interval. With many shown together, some intervals will exclude zero by chance alone. Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA): later seasons are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows in mountain terrain, which may shift NDVI without any change on the ground. The windows were fixed before the MODIS values were read; other windows can give other slopes, which is why all registered windows are stored together.

providers.processing:lineage: Anonymous SAS-signed range reads of MOD13Q1 v6.1 NDVI and pixel reliability windows over the frozen geometry from Planetary Computer (584 Terra composites); CHIRPS v3.0 monthly windows; growing-season means per pixel; stratum means weighted by 10 m analysis cells; least squares fits and trend intervals (science/pipeline/restrend-bundle.py, trend_stats.py).

restrend_long_record.title: Summary: rainfall slopes and residual trends with intervals per stratum and window (the result read_recipe_result returns)

restrend_tables.title: Full tables: every season value, window rainfall, residual, fit and sensitivity, both reliability sets

siterra:dataset.access_route: https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1 collection modis-13Q1-061, assets 250m_16_days_NDVI and 250m_16_days_pixel_reliability, anonymous SAS-signed COG range reads
siterra:dataset.resolution_note: Native 250 m MODIS sinusoidal grid (231.66 m cells), 16-day composites; rainfall on the 0.05 degree CHIRPS v3.0 grid

siterra:geo_selection.area_method: Count of 10 m analysis pixels whose centres fall inside the frozen polygon, EPSG:32629

parameters.fit_on_stored_values: NDVI season values stored at 5 decimals and rainfall at 2; fits use the stored values

operation_order: NDVI(p, c) = DN / 10000 for Terra MOD13Q1 v6.1 composite c and 250 m pixel p, kept only where the composite's pixel reliability is 0 (good) or 1 (marginal) and -0.2 <= NDVI <= 1.0; reliability 2 (snow or ice), 3 (cloudy) and fill are not observed

Composites of season y and growing window W: the 16-day composite periods of the MODIS calendar (start days of year 1, 17, ..., 353) that start in a month of W in year y; a period with no Terra product in the archive read counts as a composite with nothing kept and is listed in the result
G(p, y, W) = mean of the kept NDVI(p, c) over the season's composites, defined only when at least half of the season's composite periods (rounded up) are kept at p
w_s(p) = number of 10 m analysis cells of stratum s whose centre falls in pixel p; the catchment is the stratum of all analysis cells
Y_s(y, W) = sum over p of w_s(p) G(p, y, W) / sum over p of w_s(p), over the pixels where G is defined; withheld when those pixels hold less than 70% of the stratum's weight

P_s(y, R) = rainfall total over rainfall window R ending in season y: for each month of R, the CHIRPS v3.0 monthly values of the 0.05 degree cells weighted by the number of 10 m analysis cells of stratum s whose centre falls in each cell, summed over the months
Rainfall fit: Y = a + b P by ordinary least squares over the n seasons with both values; b is reported with its 95% interval from the t distribution with n - 2 degrees of freedom, and R squared
e(y) = Y(y) - (a + b P(y)), the rainfall-adjusted residual of season y
Residual trend d = ordinary least squares slope of e on the season year (NDVI per year), with the 95% t interval (n - 2 degrees of freedom)

Autocorrelation-adjusted interval: the same slope with standard error scaled by sqrt((n - 2) / (n_eff - 2)), n_eff = n (1 - r1) / (1 + r1), r1 the lag-1 autocorrelation of the trend-fit residuals, n_eff = n when r1 <= 0, t quantile with n_eff - 2 degrees of freedom; withheld when n_eff < 3 (Santer et al. 2000)

Theil-Sen slope of e on the season year (median of pairwise slopes) with Sen's 95% interval from the ranks (N - C) / 2 and (N + C) / 2 + 1 of the N sorted pairwise slopes, C = 1.96 sqrt(n (n - 1) (2n + 5) / 18), no tie correction (Sen 1968)
Side by side: the ordinary least squares slope and 95% t interval of Y alone (unadjusted greenness) and of P alone (rainfall) on the season year

Precondition: when the 95% interval of b does not lie entirely above zero, the result for that stratum and window pair is labelled precondition_not_met; the residual trend is still stored but is not described as rainfall-adjusted
Direction wording: an interval entirely above zero is described as upward, entirely below zero as downward, otherwise as including zero (no direction stated)

siterra:checks.name: recompute_sample_period
siterra:checks.detail: Season 2025 (mar_jun, catchment) rerun independently: 8 composites read again from Planetary Computer with a fresh token; windows identical to the stored ones: True. Season mean resampled to the 10 m analysis grid by nearest neighbour and averaged over the catchment cells: 0.220027 against the stored 0.22004 (tolerance 0.0001); coverage 1.0000 against 1.0000 (tolerance 0.001). Rainfall: catchment window totals from 10 m cell weights against the published area weights of bundle_chirps_monthly_ait_bouguemez (rainfall-cells.geojson), largest relative difference 0.0015% over every window and season (tolerance 2%).

siterra:checks.name: nodata_not_zero
siterra:checks.detail: NDVI fill (-3000) and values outside -0.2 to 1.0 are not observed; pixel reliability other than [0, 1] (primary) or [0] (sensitivity), including fill 255, is not observed; a composite period absent from Planetary Computer counts as nothing kept. A missing CHIRPS month or cell leaves the window total undefined.

siterra:checks.name: units_and_scale
siterra:checks.detail: Every stored NDVI window is int16 with nodata -3000 and GDAL scale 10000 (physical value = DN / 10000), and every item's raster:bands scale is 0.0001. Pixel reliability windows are uint8 with nodata 255, except 4 stored as int8 with nodata -1 (the product's own fill); classes 0 to 3 mean the same in both, and only listed classes are kept. Rainfall in mm per window.

siterra:checks.name: qa_join_coverage
siterra:checks.detail: All 584 composites share one window grid for NDVI and pixel reliability (176 x 131 pixels); stratum weights count 10 m analysis cells per MODIS pixel and per CHIRPS cell. In the registered growing windows: 2 composite periods absent from Planetary Computer (A2025193, A2025209); on 2026-10-28 NASA CMR listed 2 of them (held by the NASA archive, which needs an Earthdata login, not used).

siterra:checks.name: period_alignment
siterra:checks.detail: A composite belongs to a season when its 16-day period starts in a month of the growing window of that year; rainfall windows end in the season's year as configured (start and end month with year offsets).

siterra:checks.name: attribution_present
siterra:checks.detail: MOD13Q1 v6.1 citation with DOI, subset and access date, the CHIRPS v3.0 attribution and the Copernicus DEM notices are in siterra:attribution
